issues.legal_issue: A substantial interpretive dispute about the computation of vacant land under the ceiling law should be referred for consideration by a larger bench when the relevant earlier decisions conflict and a larger-bench decision bears on the dispute.
material_facts: The appeal concerned whether land occupied by a factory and land appurtenant to it had to be included when calculating the vacant land held by the landholder.
The competent authority had found vacant land in excess of the ceiling, while the appellate court disagreed with its interpretation of the statutory provisions.
The Court considered earlier decisions that addressed the computation question differently and noted that one relevant decision had been given by a three-judge bench.
The Court found force in the contention that an earlier decision had considered the provisions at issue more broadly than a later decision appeared to recognize.
issues.conclusion: The Court did not resolve the substantive computation question. It directed that the case be placed before the Chief Justice for an appropriate direction because the contention should be considered by a larger bench.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(q)(ii) and 2(q)(iii), read with Section 4(9) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976, govern the dispute over whether land occupied by a building and its appurtenant land are included in calculating vacant land. State of U.P. v. L.J. Johnson and Meera Gupta v. State of West Bengal had addressed the issue in ways that raised a conflict; Meera Gupta was decided by a three-judge bench. The Court therefore considered that the interpretive contention should be considered by a larger bench rather than deciding it in this appeal.

predicates.appeal_involves_statutory_interpretation: The proceeding is an appeal in which the application of statutory provisions to a disputed legal issue must be interpreted.
predicates.earlier_decisions_conflict: Earlier judicial decisions address the relevant interpretive issue in conflicting ways.
predicates.larger_bench_decided_related_issue: A larger bench has decided an earlier case that bears on the interpretive issue.

issues.definition: When an appeal requires statutory interpretation, earlier decisions conflict, and a larger bench has decided a related issue, the interpretive issue is referred for larger-bench consideration.
